edition.locus: De Trinitate VI (anthropomorphism; Spiritus est Deus; worship in spirit)

source_text: VI. 1. Et licet scriptura caelestis ad humanam formam faciem diuinam saepe conuertat, dum dicit: Oculi Domini super iustos, aut dum odoratus est Dominus Deus odorem bonae fragrantiae, aut dum traduntur Moysi tabulae scriptae digito Dei, aut dum populus filiorum Israel de terra Aegypti manu ualida et brachio excelso liberatur, aut dum dicit: Os enim Domini locutum est haec, aut dum terra scabellum pedum Dei esse perhibetur, aut dum dicit: Inclina aurem tuam et audi, sed nos qui dicimus quia lex spiritalis est, non intra haec nostri corporis lineamenta modum aut figuram diuinae maiestatis includimus, sed suis illam interminatae magnitudinis, ut ita dixerim, campis sine ullo fine diffundimus. 2. Scriptum est enim: Si ascendero in caelum, tu ibi es; si descendero ad inferos, ades; et si assumpsero alas meas et abiero trans mare, ibi manus tua apprehendet me et dextera tua detinebit me. Rationem enim diuinae scripturae de temperamento dispositionis cognoscimus. Parabolis enim adhuc secundum fidei tempus de Deo prophetes tunc loquebatur, non quomodo Deus erat, sed quomodo populus capere poterat. Vt igitur haec sic de Deo dicantur, non Deo, sed populo potius imputetur. 3. Sic et tabernaculum erigere populo permittitur, nec tamen Deus intra tabernaculum clusus continetur. Sic et templum extruitur, nec tamen Deus intra templi angustias omnino saepitur. Non igitur mediocris est Deus, sed populi mediocris est sensus, nec angustus Deus, sed rationis populi angustus est intellectus habitus. 4. Denique in euangelio Veniet hora, Dominus aiebat, cum neque in monte isto neque in Hierusalem adorabitis Patrem. Et causas reddidit dicens: Spiritus est Deus; et eos ergo qui adorant in spiritu et ueritate adorare oportet. 5. Efficaciae igitur ibi diuinae per membra monstrantur, non habitus Dei nec corporalia lineamenta ponuntur. Nam et cum oculi describuntur, quod omnia uideat exprimitur. Et quando auris, quod omnia audiat proponitur. Et cum digitus, significantia quaedam uoluntatis aperitur. Et cum nares, precum quasi odorum perceptio ostenditur. Et cum manus, quod creaturae sit omnis auctor probatur. Et quando bracchium, quod nulla natura contra robur ipsius repugnare possit edicitur. Et quando pedes, quod impleat omnia nec sit quicquam ubi non sit Deus explicatur. 6. Neque enim sunt ei aut membra aut membrorum officia necessaria, ad cuius solum etiam tacitum arbitrium et seruiunt et adsunt omnia. Cur enim requirat oculos, qui lux est? Aut cur quaerat pedes, qui ubique est? Aut cur ingredi uelit, cum non sit quo extra se progredi possit? Aut cur manus expetat, cuius ad omnia instituenda artifex est et silens uoluntas? Nec auribus eget, qui etiam tacitas nouit uoluntates. Aut propter quam causam linguam quaerat, cui cogitare iussisse est? 7. Necessaria enim haec membra hominibus fuerunt, non Deo, quia inefficax hominis consilium fuisset, nisi cogitamen corpus implesset, Deo autem non necessaria, cuius uoluntatem non tantum sine aliqua molitione opera subsequuntur, sed ipsa statim opera cum uoluntate procedunt. 8. Ceterum ipse totus oculus, quia totus uidet, et totus auris, quia totus audit, et totus manus, quia totus operatur, et totus pes, quia totus ubique est. Idem enim, quicquid illud est, totus aequalis est et totus ubique est. 9. Non enim habet in se diuersitatem sui quicquid est simplex. Ea enim demum in diuersitatem membrorum recidunt quae ueniunt ex natiuitate in dissolutionem. Sed haec quae concreta non sunt sentire non possunt. Quod enim immortale est, quicquid est, illud ipsum unum et simplex et semper est. Et ideo quia unum est, dissolui non potest, quoniam quicquid est illud ipsum extra ius dissolutionis positum, legibus est mortis solutum.
pass_a_gloss: Scripture’s bodily words about God show divine workings, not a bodily outline; God is Spirit, whole eye/ear/hand/foot, to be worshiped in spirit and truth.
pass_b_english: VI. 1. And although heavenly Scripture often turns the divine face toward human form when it says: The eyes of the Lord are upon the just, or when the Lord God smelled a smell of good fragrance, or when tablets written by God’s finger are handed to Moses, or when the people of Israel’s sons is freed from Egypt’s land by a strong hand and lofty arm, or when it says: For the Lord’s mouth has spoken these things, or when the earth is asserted to be the footstool of God’s feet, or when it says: Incline your ear and hear — yet we who say that the law is spiritual do not enclose the measure or figure of divine majesty within these outlines of our body, but pour it out, so to speak, upon its own fields of unbounded greatness without any end. 2. For it is written: If I ascend into heaven, you are there; if I descend to the underworld, you are present; and if I take my wings and go across the sea, there your hand will seize me and your right hand will hold me. For we know Scripture’s reason about the tempering of arrangement. For by parables still according to faith’s time the prophet then spoke about God, not as God was, but as the people could take. Therefore that these things are so said about God should be charged not to God but rather to the people. 3. So also the people is permitted to raise a tabernacle, and yet God is not shut contained within the tabernacle. So also a temple is built, and yet God is not at all fenced within the temple’s narrows. God therefore is not mediocre, but the people’s sense is mediocre; nor is God narrow, but the people’s reason has a narrow understanding. 4. Finally in the Gospel the Lord said: The hour will come when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. And he gave reasons saying: God is Spirit; and those who worship must therefore worship in spirit and truth. 5. Therefore divine workings are shown there through members; God’s habit and bodily outlines are not set. For when eyes are described, it is expressed that he sees all. And when an ear, it is put forward that he hears all. And when a finger, a certain signifying of will is opened. And when nostrils, perception of prayers as of odors is shown. And when a hand, it is proved that he is author of every creature. And when an arm, it is declared that no nature can fight against his strength. And when feet, it is unfolded that he fills all things and there is nothing where God is not. 6. For neither are members or members’ offices necessary to him, to whose even silent judgment alone all things both serve and are present. For why would he require eyes, who is light? Or why seek feet, who is everywhere? Or why wish to walk, when there is nowhere he can go forward outside himself? Or why demand hands, whose silent will is craftsman for establishing all things? Nor does he need ears, who knows even silent wills. Or for what cause would he seek a tongue, for whom to think is to have commanded? 7. For these members were necessary for men, not for God, because man’s counsel would have been ineffective unless the body filled out the thought; but not necessary for God, whose works not only follow the will without any effort, but the works themselves proceed at once with the will. 8. For the rest he himself is all eye, because he wholly sees, and all ear, because he wholly hears, and all hand, because he wholly works, and all foot, because he is wholly everywhere. For the same one, whatever that is, is wholly equal and wholly everywhere. 9. For whatever is simple does not have diversity of itself in itself. For those things finally fall into diversity of members which come from birth into dissolution. But these things which are not compacted cannot sense. For whatever is immortal, whatever it is, that itself is one and simple and always. And therefore because it is one, it cannot be dissolved, since whatever that itself is, placed outside dissolution’s right, is loosed from death’s laws.

lemmas.sense: law is spiritual; God not shut in body outlines
members name workings, not bodily habit

choices.choose: Bodily words for God name his workings; they do not enclose him in flesh’s outline
reject: God has literal bodily members like a creature
choices.why: efficaciae per membra; non habitus Dei; lex spiritalis.

choices.choose: God is Spirit, to be worshiped in spirit and truth, wholly present and simple
reject: Worship is tied to place or a composite bodily God
